metadata.description: A manager-driven multi-agent pipeline where a large-context Architect produces a structured design dossier, an Orchestrator decomposes and routes work, smaller-context Coder agents implement in isolated git worktrees, and a Verifier gates every merge. The pipeline uses a nested-loop control structure (inner action loop + outer reflection loop) modeled on Magentic-One, with a durable task board and typed handoff envelopes modeled on production agent-engineering practice.

design_principles.principle: Authority attenuates down the tree: child ⊆ parent ∩ role.
Every handoff is typed, versioned, and validated against a schema.
State lives in a durable ledger, not in chat history.
Workers are stateless; failed attempts leave zero trace.
Free-form prose is untrusted data; only typed fields drive routing.

outer_loop.name: reflection
outer_loop.action: The Orchestrator writes a reflection entry to the ledger: what went wrong, what was learned, and a revised plan. The task ledger is updated before the next inner-loop cycle begins.

steps.step: Select highest-priority pending task matching role.
Dispatch to worker with isolated execution context.
Collect typed result; update ledger atomically.
Increment or reset stall counter based on progress signal.

role.mission: Own the ledger, decompose goals, route typed work, detect stalls, and enforce invariants.

instructions.critical_constraint: The Orchestrator MUST NOT write or edit source files. It only coordinates; implementation authority belongs to coders.
Every dispatch MUST include a schema-valid handoff envelope. If validation fails, the task returns to pending with failure code HANDOFF_INVALID.
The Orchestrator MUST maintain a stall counter per active task and trigger reflection when progress signals are absent for two consecutive cycles.

role.mission: Produce a complete, structured design dossier and a dependency-ordered task plan.

instructions.critical_constraint: The Architect MUST produce three artifacts: ARCHITECTURE.md, requirements.json, and file_tree.json. Markdown carries rationale; JSON carries machine-parseable structure.
Every task in the plan MUST declare: goal, acceptance_criteria, constraints, context_refs, output_format, dependencies, and estimated_blast_radius.

artifact.purpose: Human-readable design rationale, trade-offs, and module boundaries.
Planned file paths, modes, and change notes for coders.
Dependency-ordered task graph conforming to task-plan.schema.json.

role.mission: Implement exactly one delegated task inside an isolated worktree and return a typed result.

isolation.invariant: Never touch the main checkout or another task's worktree.

instructions.critical_constraint: The Coder MUST treat the handoff envelope as the single source of truth. It MUST NOT infer additional scope from free-form prose.
Before editing, the Coder MUST validate that every required field in the envelope is present. Missing fields return HANDOFF_INCOMPLETE immediately.
The Coder MUST return both a human-readable summary and a machine-readable result block fenced by RESULT_START / RESULT_END.

role.mission: Independently validate implementation results against acceptance criteria and return a typed verdict.

instructions.critical_constraint: The Verifier MUST evaluate only evidence: diff, test output, and acceptance criteria. It MUST NOT rely on the Coder's summary alone.
A rejection MUST include actionable feedback items, each with severity, file, and fix_hint.
Rejection cycles are capped at 3. After the cap, the task escalates to the Orchestrator with status retry_cap.

handoff-contracts.description: Every inter-agent message uses a typed envelope. The envelope is the contract; free-form prose is carried as an untrusted payload and never drives routing decisions.

invariants.invariant: handoff_id + nonce are single-use; replay returns already_claimed

example.objective: Implement the JWT refresh endpoint in src/auth/refresh.ts according to the interface contract in artifacts/requirements.json.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Endpoint returns 200 with a new access token for a valid refresh token.
Expired or revoked refresh tokens return 401 with code TOKEN_INVALID.
Unit tests cover both success and failure paths; coverage ≥ 90% for the new module.

constraints.constraint: Do not modify the public API of src/auth/index.ts.
Use the existing TokenStore interface; do not introduce a new dependency.

guards.guard: Handoff envelope MUST validate against handoff-envelope.schema.json.
Verifier verdict MUST be PASS and diff_digest MUST match the published commit.
Verifier feedback MUST contain at least one feedback-item.

format.usage: Roles, model tiers, tool allowlists, routing rules, retry thresholds.

example.code: roles: coder: model: small-context tools: [file.read, file.write, file.edit, shell.exec, test.run] accepts: [implementation, bug_fix, revision] routes_to: [verifier] max_instances: 3

format.usage: ARCHITECTURE.md, design decision records, rejection feedback, final summaries.
format.why: Markdown is the native reasoning format of LLMs and the lingua franca of engineering documentation.

format.usage: Handoff envelopes, task plans, requirements, results, ledger snapshots.
format.rule: Every JSON artifact MUST declare its schema version and validate on write and read.

format.usage: Role definitions, constraints, output contracts, few-shot examples.
format.rule: Use consistent, descriptive tags; nest for hierarchy; keep prose inside the smallest applicable tag.

mechanism.name: git-worktree-per-task
mechanism.invariant: Main checkout is never mutated directly.
mechanism.cleanup: On failure, discard worktree and branch; retry begins from a clean base.

authority.invariant: Orchestrator and Verifier are read-only with respect to source files.
Coder authority is scoped to the allocated worktree and the allowed_tools list.
A child handoff cannot carry broader tool access than its parent envelope.

budget.invariant: Every handoff declares step, time, and cost budgets.
The sum of sibling reservations cannot exceed the parent budget.

replay_protection.invariant: handoff_id and nonce are single-use; replay returns already_claimed without re-execution.
Coder results are idempotent by task_id; duplicate completion is a no-op.

quality_gates.gate: Handoff envelope validates; required fields present; budget > 0.
Verifier verdict = PASS; tests_passed = true; diff_digest matches published commit.
All downstream dependencies are terminal; no unresolved retry_cap tasks.

configuration-template.code:
pipeline: name: architect-coder-orchestration max_wall_clock_minutes: 120 stall_threshold: 2 reflection_max_iterations: 3
roles: orchestrator: model: large-context write_access: none allowed_tools: [task-board.*, ledger.write, envelope.validate, worktree.allocate] architect: model: large-context write_access: artifact-only allowed_tools: [read.repository, read.design-artifacts, write.design-artifacts] coder: model: small-context multiplicity: 3 write_access: worktree-scoped allowed_tools: [file.*, shell.exec, test.run, git.commit] verifier: model: large-context write_access: none allowed_tools: [diff.read, test.run, artifact.read]
guardrails: max_task_depth: 10 max_tasks_per_group: 50 max_rejections_per_task: 3 max_added_lines_per_attempt: 500
schemas: handoff: schemas/handoff-envelope.schema.json task_plan: schemas/task-plan.schema.json coder_result: schemas/coder-result.schema.json

extension-points.extension: Insert new roles between architect and coder (e.g., security-reviewer, migration-specialist). The role must declare accepts, routes_to, allowed_tools, and a result schema.
The YAML configuration can swap the model provider for any role without changing the orchestration graph or handoff contracts.
Any state can transition to awaiting_human via the Orchestrator. A human approval produces a typed approval envelope that satisfies the pre_merge gate.
